summary: 94/308 supplies plural predicative ṣṭime with kefe and degree ġalabe. The adjectival hardness meaning is secure from the Turoyo nominal frame and context; membership in the ṣṭm verbal paradigm is not.

The reader reports an independent dictionary adjective ṣṭimo hart (Stein). This supports the adjective meaning but not the proposed verbal Detransitive derivation; that dictionary is not independently consulted beyond the permitted input.

Ṣṭim bayto at 96/212 is a fixed malediction already represented under Detransitive Preterit. Preserve that inherited classification provisionally rather than repeat its quotation as a new example or claim a freely productive curse paradigm.
The input has no separately worded Detransitive sense list although its existing example is filed in a Detransitive box; D1 in the reader record corresponds to that existing unnumbered use.
Is ṣṭimo hard a lexical adjective independent of ṣṭm, or a demonstrable Detransitive Part. Pass.? Obtain a paradigm or explicit native judgment before adding the stone use to the verb inventory.
How productive is Ṣṭim bayto as a Detransitive clause versus a frozen curse? Keep the inherited box until this is decided.
